name: Describe an image aloud
description: Describe an image so a person who cannot see it knows what is there and what you are guessing.
l1c: Describe the main subject of an image in two sentences a listener can check if they look later.
l1d: You can say what an image shows.
l2c: Mark one thing you are inferring, such as a mood or a place, and one thing you can actually see.
l2d: You can tell sight from guess.
l3c: Answer one question about the image, or say the image does not show it.
l3d: You can use the description for a real question.
safety: Do not name a private person who did not agree. This is not a certified audio-description course.

name: Rewrite a notice in plain language
description: Rewrite a short official notice so a reader can say what they must do.
l1c: Underline what the reader is supposed to do, and by when, if a time is printed.
l1d: You can find the action in a notice.
l2c: Rewrite that action in words a friend can repeat, without adding a rule that was not in the notice.
l3c: Ask someone what they would do next, and fix the sentence if they name the wrong action.
l3d: You can test plain language on a person.
safety: Do not change a legal meaning. If you are unsure, keep the original beside the rewrite.

name: Check whether a sign can be read
description: Look at a sign and say whether the words can be read from the place a person would stand.
l1c: Stand where a reader would stand and read the sign aloud, or say which word you cannot read.
l1d: You can test a sign in place.
l2c: Say whether the problem is size, contrast, glare, or something in the way.
l2d: You can name why a sign fails.
l3c: Propose one change, such as a darker pen or a move out of the glare, and show a version you can read.
l3d: You can improve a sign you control.
safety: Do not climb to reach a sign. Do not alter a sign you do not own.

name: Write alt text you can check
description: Write alternative text that matches the image and leaves out a guess.
l1c: Write one sentence of alt text that names the subject.
l2c: Remove any claim about why the person is there or how they feel, unless the image states it.
l2d: You can keep alt text factual.
l3c: Read the alt text to someone who is not looking, then show the image and fix one miss.
l3d: You can test alt text by ear.
safety: Use only an image you may describe.

name: Offer a seated version of a task
description: Show how a standing task can be done from a chair, or say that it cannot.
l1c: Do one ordinary task from a chair, such as folding, reading, or sorting, and note what you cannot reach.
l1d: You can try a task seated.
l2c: Bring the materials into reach, or say which part still needs standing.
l3c: Offer the seated version and the standing version, and use the one the person chooses.
l3d: You can let the person choose.
safety: Do not lift someone. Stop if they feel unsteady.

name: Find a step-free way
description: Find a way into a place that does not use a step, using signs you can see.
l1c: Find the step-free entrance sign, or say you cannot find one from where you are.
l1d: You can look for a step-free way.
l2c: Follow the signs to the entrance and stop if the route is blocked.
l3c: Describe the route in two sentences, including where it failed if it did.
safety: Do not use a lift in a fire alarm. This is not a building survey.

name: Caption a short clip
description: Add words to a short clip so a viewer can read what is said.
l1c: Write the spoken words of a few seconds you are allowed to caption.
l1d: You can transcribe a short clip.
l2c: Show the words while those sounds are heard, not after the clip has moved on.
l3c: Add one non-speech sound that matters, such as a door, or say there was none.
l3d: You can include a meaningful sound.
safety: Caption only media you may use. Do not invent dialogue.

name: Slow your speech when asked
description: Slow down and repeat a sentence when a listener asks, without adding new content.
l1c: When asked, repeat the same sentence more slowly.
l2c: Split the sentence into two parts and pause between them.
l3c: Ask the listener to say back the part they needed, and repeat only that part if they missed it.
l3d: You can repair the missed part.
safety: Do not patronize. Follow the listener's ask.

name: Read a program note
description: Read a program note and say what the performance says it is, separate from your opinion.
l1c: Point to the title and one sentence about what the audience will see or hear.
l2c: Write one fact from the note and one reaction that is yours.
l2d: You can tell the note from your taste.
l3c: During or after the event, name one thing the note prepared you to notice.
l3d: You can use a note as a lens.
safety: Use a program you were given. Do not record a performance unless it is allowed.

name: Compare two objects in a gallery
description: Compare two objects using what you can see and what their labels say.
l1c: Choose two objects and say one visible difference.
l2c: Add one difference that comes from the labels, such as date or place.
l2d: You can add the label to the look.
l3c: Write one comparison you cannot settle from the objects and the labels.
l3d: You can stop where the evidence stops.
safety: Do not touch objects unless the gallery says you may. A museum label skill already exists; this one compares two objects.

name: Notice a repeated motif
description: Find a shape, color, or phrase that repeats in a place or a work, and say where it returns.
l1c: Point to a motif and to the second place it appears.
l2c: Say what is the same and what changes the second time.
l3c: Say what job the repeat might be doing, and mark that sentence as your guess.
l3d: You can interpret without pretending it is a fact.
safety: None.

name: Give a three-stop tour
description: Guide someone through three stops you know, with one true fact at each.
l1c: Pick three stops and one fact you can point to at each.
l1d: You can plan a short tour.
l2c: Take a person to the three stops in order and say the fact at the place.
l3c: When they ask something you do not know, say so, and do not invent a date or a name.
l3d: You can keep a tour honest.
safety: Stay on public ground. Do not enter a private space.

name: Read a building facade
description: Describe a building from the street by its door, windows, and material.
l1c: Point to the entrance, one window pattern, and the main material.
l1d: You can look at a facade.
l2c: Say which part shows you how to enter, and which is only decoration if you can tell.
l2d: You can separate use from decoration.
l3c: Write one thing you cannot know without going inside or reading a source.
l3d: You can limit a street reading.
safety: Do not enter a site that is closed. Do not climb.

name: Note one choice in a performance
description: Watch or listen to a live performance and name one choice the performers made.
l1c: Watch or listen to one section without checking a phone, and name what happened.
l1d: You can attend to a section.
l2c: Name one choice, such as a pause, a repeat, or where someone stood.
l3c: Say what that choice did for you, and mark it as your response.
l3d: You can tell a choice from your reaction.
safety: Follow the venue's recording rules.

name: Find who made an object
description: Find the maker or the source of an object from a mark, a label, or a catalog.
l1c: Look for a signature, a label, or a stamp, and write what it says or that there is none.
l2c: If there is a name or a number, look it up in the place's list or catalog.
l3c: Write whether you found a person, a workshop, or only a number, and what you still do not know.
l3d: You can report a partial find.
safety: Do not remove a label.

name: Read an exhibition map
description: Use a gallery map to find a room and a work, then the way back.
l1c: Point to where you are on the map and to the room you want.
l1d: You can orient on a gallery map.
l2c: Go to the room and find the work number the map or list names.
l2d: You can use the map to arrive.
l3c: Use the map to name the way back to the entrance.
l3d: You can leave by the map.
safety: This is not a topographic map skill. Follow gallery directions if the map and the staff disagree.

name: Prepare one question for a guide
description: Prepare a question a guide can answer from the place, and ask it.
l1c: Write one question that is not a request for a private story.
l2c: Ask it, let the guide finish, and write the answer in their sense.
l3c: If they cannot answer, write that, and do not fill the gap yourself.
l3d: You can leave a question open.
safety: Do not record the guide without asking.

name: Show a lever at work
description: Use a lever to lift a light load and say where the pivot is.
l1c: Set a ruler or a bar on a pivot and lift a small object.
l1d: You can make a lever lift.
l2c: Move the pivot and say whether the lift felt easier or harder.
l3c: Point to a door handle, a bottle opener, or another everyday lever and name the pivot.
l3d: You can see a lever outside the experiment.
safety: Use a light object. Do not put fingers under the load.

name: Compare how cups hold heat
description: Compare two cups of warm water and say which stays warmer, without a medical claim.
l1c: Pour the same warm water into two different cups and note the time.
l1d: You can set a fair comparison.
l2c: After the same wait, feel or measure both and say which is warmer.
l3c: Name one way the test was not fair, such as a different amount or a draft.
safety: Use water you can touch. Do not use boiling water. This is not a materials certificate.

name: Test what floats
description: Test small objects in water and sort them by whether they float.
l1c: Place small objects in a bowl of water and sort them into floats and sinks.
l2c: Change the shape of one material, such as a flat sheet and a boat, and say what changed.
l2d: You can see that shape matters.
l3n: Refuse a rule that is too big
l3c: Write one rule you will not claim, because you tested only these objects.
l3d: You can keep the conclusion small.
safety: Do not test electrical objects. Do not leave water where it can spill into a socket.

name: Find the poles of a magnet
description: Find which ends of two magnets attract and which resist.
l1c: Bring two magnets together and show an end that resists.
l2c: Mark the ends that attract each other and check the mark a second time.
l3c: Predict whether two marked ends will attract or resist, then test it.
safety: Keep magnets away from cards, screens, and medical devices.

name: Track a shadow
description: Mark a shadow twice and say how it moved.
l1c: Mark the tip of a shadow and the time.
l2c: Mark it later and say which way the tip moved.
l3n: Say what you did not measure
l3c: Say that this does not give a clock or a compass bearing by itself, and why.
safety: Do not look at the sun. Weather recording is a different skill.

name: Balance a hanging mobile
description: Hang two objects so a stick hangs level.
l1c: Suspend a stick from one point and see which side drops.
l2c: Move an object or add a small one until the stick hangs level.
l3c: Move one object, show the tilt, and restore the level.
safety: Hang it where it cannot fall on a person. Use light objects.

name: Bounce light with a mirror
description: Use a mirror to send a patch of light to a target you chose.
l1c: Use a mirror to put a patch of daylight or a lamp on a wall.
l2c: Move the mirror until the patch sits on a target you marked.
l3c: Say what happens when the light source is blocked, and do not claim a rule about lasers.
l3d: You can see that the patch needs a source.
safety: Do not reflect the sun into anyone's eyes. Do not use a laser.

name: Separate a simple mixture
description: Separate a mixture of two safe materials with a sieve or a magnet.
l1c: Look at a mixture of two safe materials and say whether you will use a sieve or a magnet, and why.
l2c: Carry out that method and show two piles that are mostly one material each.
l3c: Point to what is still mixed and say you are not claiming a pure sample.
l3d: You can see the leftover mix.
safety: Use dry food, sand, paper, or paperclips. No chemicals.

name: Time a pendulum
description: Time a swinging weight and see what happens when you change the length.
l1c: Time a counted run of swings of the same pendulum and write the time.
l2c: Change only the length, time the same count, and say which was slower.
l3c: Say one thing you did not change, such as the weight, so you do not claim it was tested.
l3d: You can name the uncontrolled part.
safety: Use a soft weight. Keep the swing away from faces.

name: Send sound along a string
description: Send a voice along a tight string and show that a slack string fails.
l1c: Stretch a string between two cups or cans and speak quietly into one.
l1d: You can set up the line.
l2c: Have someone hear the other end, then slacken the string and try again.
l2d: You can show the tight string matters.
l3c: Say one reason this is not a telephone, such as distance or a broken line.
safety: Do not use glass that can cut. Do not tie the line across a path.

name: Test which cloth soaks water
description: Compare two cloths by how they take up a spoon of water.
l1c: Put the same small amount of water on two cloths.
l1d: You can keep the test fair.
l2c: Say which cloth spread or held the water more, and show it.
l3c: Say which you would put under a wet cup, and one reason the test might not match a real spill.
l3d: You can use the test and limit it.
safety: Use water only.

name: Pick up paper with static
description: Charge a balloon or a comb and pick up a small piece of paper, then say when it stops.
l1c: Rub a balloon or a comb on dry hair or cloth and lift a bit of paper.
l1d: You can make static lift paper.
l2c: Touch the balloon to a wall or wait, and show that the paper no longer jumps.
l2d: You can see the effect end.
l3c: Say one condition that made it weak, such as damp air, or say you could not tell.
safety: Keep this away from faces and from medical devices.

name: Compare two ramps
description: Roll the same object down two ramps and say which was faster or farther.
l1c: Roll the same object down one ramp and mark where it stops.
l2c: Change the height or the surface, roll again, and say what changed.
l3c: Repeat the better trial and say whether the result held.
safety: Use a light ball. Keep it out of a walkway.

name: Feel which handle warms
description: Put two spoons in warm water and say which handle warms first.
l1c: Put a metal spoon and a wooden or plastic spoon in the same warm water.
l2c: After a short wait, feel the handles and say which is warmer.
l3c: Say you compared handles, not a rule for every material.
l3d: You can keep the claim narrow.
safety: Use water you can touch, not boiling water.

name: Build a glossary for a topic
description: Collect words for one topic, each with a meaning in your own words.
l1c: Choose one topic and write several words with meanings you could explain aloud.
l2c: Use one of the words in a sentence about a real source you read.
l3c: If two entries overlap, merge them or say how they differ.
safety: Do not copy a long definition. A short meaning in your words is enough.

name: Index a notebook
description: Make an index so you can find a note by topic.
l1c: List the topics in a notebook you use and the page or date of one note for each.
l2c: Use the index to find one note without flipping at random.
l2d: You can retrieve from the index.
l3c: Add a new note to the index the same day, or mark the index as behind.
l3d: You can keep an index current.
safety: None.

name: Trace a number to its source
description: Take a number from a text and find the source it cites, or say the source is missing.
l1c: Point to a number and the sentence that uses it.
l2c: Find the citation, link, or table the sentence points to, or write that there is none.
l3c: If you found the source, say whether the number matches, or that you could not open it.
l3d: You can check or admit the gap.
safety: Do not invent a source. Chart reading is a different skill.

name: Compare a headline with the text
description: Compare a headline with the first part of the article and say what the headline added or left out.
l1c: Read the headline and the opening of the article.
l2c: Name one claim in the headline that the opening does or does not support.
l3c: Write a plainer headline that matches the opening, and mark it as yours.
safety: Comparing two full accounts is a different skill. This one stays with one article.

name: File a clipping with a date
description: Save a short clipping with its date and where it came from.
l1c: Save a clipping or a link you are allowed to keep.
l2c: Write the date and the publication or the page.
l3c: Find it again from the date or the topic, and fix the label if you could not.
safety: Do not save private material you were not given.

name: Keep a source log
description: Log each source you open for one question, including the ones that did not help.
l1c: Write the question before you open a source.
l2c: Log two sources with a line on whether each helped.
l3c: Keep one source that did not answer, and say why you are not citing it.
l3d: You can show a dead end.
safety: Citing a source in a note is a different skill. This one is the log of the search.

name: Turn a table into a sentence
description: Write one sentence a table supports, and one it does not.
l1c: Say what the columns or rows are.
l1d: You can read a table's frame.
l2c: Write one sentence and point to the cells it uses.
l2d: You can speak from the cells.
l3c: Write a sentence a reader might think the table says, and show that the cells do not say it.
safety: Reading a chart is a different skill.

name: Write a correction
description: Correct something you said or wrote, in the same place the mistake went.
l1c: Point to the sentence that was wrong and say what was wrong.
l2c: Write the correction where the original readers can see it.
l3c: Keep the old line visible or marked, so the change can be seen.
l3d: You can correct without hiding the history.
safety: Do not erase someone else's record.

name: Run a brainstorm
description: Collect ideas from a group before anyone ranks them.
l1c: Write one question and say that ranking comes later.
l2c: Write every idea offered, and stop a critique until the list is done.
l3c: Read the list back and say which step, such as clustering, has not happened yet.
safety: Do not force anyone to speak.

name: Cluster a list of ideas
description: Group a list of ideas by similarity and name each group.
l1c: Put ideas that belong together into piles, and leave one aside if it fits nowhere.
l2c: Give each pile a name the group can accept.
l3c: Split a pile that hides two topics, or merge two piles that are the same, and say which you did.
safety: None.

name: Use a dot vote
description: Let a group mark preferences with a limited number of dots, then read the result.
l1c: Say how many dots each person gets and that a dot is a preference, not a decision by itself.
l2c: Count the dots in front of the group.
l3n: Say what it does not decide
l3c: Say what the dots did not settle, such as who will do the work.
l3d: You can limit a dot vote.
safety: Agree the rule before anyone marks.

name: Park a topic
description: Set aside an off-topic point without losing it.
l1c: Write the off-topic point in a parking place the group can see.
l1d: You can capture a side point.
l2c: Go back to the question you were on.
l2d: You can leave the side point.
l3c: At the end, either schedule the parked point or say it will not be taken up, and mark which.
l3d: You can close a parked point.
safety: Running a full meeting is a different skill.

name: Switch roles in a pair
description: Do a task in a pair, then switch who leads and who checks.
l1c: Say who leads and who checks before you start.
l2c: Switch roles for the next part of the task.
l3c: Each person says one thing they noticed in the other role.
l3d: You can learn from the switch.
safety: Do not switch into a dangerous task.

name: Debrief a task
description: After a task, say what worked, what failed, and one change.
l1c: State what the task produced, in a sentence.
l1d: You can start from the result.
l2c: Name one thing that failed and one that worked.
l3c: Choose one change for next time and who will remember it.
l3d: You can leave with a change.
safety: A weekly review is a different skill. This one follows a single task.

name: Stop at a timebox
description: Work until a time you set, then stop and say what is unfinished.
l1c: Write the end time before you start.
l2c: Stop at that time even if you want to continue.
l3c: Write what is unfinished, separate from what is done.
safety: A focus block is a different skill. This one is about stopping a group or a task.

name: Ask for a dissent
description: Ask whether anyone sees the decision differently, and record that view.
l1c: After a proposal, ask if anyone disagrees or is unsure.
l2c: Write the dissenting point without arguing it down in the same breath.
l3n: Say what you did with it
l3c: Say whether the decision changed, or that it stood and the dissent remains noted.
l3d: You can show the fate of the dissent.
safety: Do not require a name if the person wants the point recorded without one.

name: Cross to a mark
description: Walk to a marked spot on a cue and stop there.
l1c: Mark a spot and walk to it from a start line.
l2c: Start on a cue word and arrive as the line ends.
l3c: If you arrive early or late, change your start and show the better cross.
safety: Keep the path clear. This is not stage combat.

name: Take a cue
description: Enter or speak when a cue happens, not before.
l1c: Agree the cue, a word or an action, before the run.
l2c: Stay still until the cue, then do the action.
l3c: If you miss it, take the next agreed chance or stop and reset, and say which.
safety: None.

name: Be heard at the back of a room
description: Speak so a person at the back can repeat your sentence, without straining.
l1c: Speak one sentence to a person at the back of the room.
l2c: Ask them to repeat it, and try once more if they missed a word.
l3c: If your throat tightens, stop and say you would rest rather than push.
safety: Stop if it hurts. Public speaking as a talk is a different skill.

name: Show a prop
description: Hold an object so a watcher can see it, then pass or set it down on purpose.
l1c: Hold the object still long enough for a watcher to say what it is.
l2c: Turn it if they say a hand is covering it, and show it again.
l3c: Set it on an agreed place so the next person can find it.
safety: Do not use a sharp or hot object.

name: Leave a pause
description: Pause on purpose in a spoken line, and say what the pause did.
l1c: Choose a place in a short text to pause.
l2c: Speak the text and hold the pause long enough that a listener notices.
l3c: Ask the listener what they thought the pause was for, and say whether that matched your aim.
safety: Reading aloud for comprehension is a different skill.

name: Warm up your voice
description: Do a short gentle voice warm-up and stop if anything hurts.
l1c: Hum or speak a simple pattern quietly for a short time.
l2c: Repeat a little louder and say whether it feels easy.
l3c: Name the signal that would stop you, such as pain or a tickle, and stop if it appears.
safety: Pain means stop. This is not a singing lesson and not medical advice. Matching pitch is a different skill.

name: Move a simple puppet
description: Move a simple puppet so a watcher can tell where it is looking.
l1c: Hold the puppet still and point its face at one spot.
l2c: Move it as if it speaks one line, then still it when the line ends.
l3c: Ask a watcher where it was looking, and adjust if they say the wrong place.
safety: Use a soft puppet. No stage machinery.

name: Make a flipbook
description: Draw a flipbook in which one thing moves when the pages turn.
l1c: Draw a simple change across several pages, such as a dot moving.
l2c: Flip the pages and show that the motion reads.
l3c: Find a page where the motion jumps, redraw it, and show the smoother flip.
safety: None.

name: Make a short stop-motion
description: Move an object a little between photos so it appears to move.
l1c: Take a series of photos, moving the object a little each time.
l2c: Play the frames in order and say what action they show.
l3c: Reshoot the frame where the object jumps too far.
safety: Do not include people who have not agreed. Filming a live clip is a different skill.

name: Draw a three-panel comic
description: Draw three panels in which something changes from the first to the third.
l1c: Write what the first and last panel show before you draw.
l2c: Draw three panels so a reader can tell the order.
l3c: Ask someone what changed, and redraw a panel if they cannot tell.
l3d: You can revise from a reader.
safety: A prose scene is a different skill. Do not depict a real person without consent.

name: Print from a soft stamp
description: Cut a simple shape in a soft eraser and print it.
l1c: Draw a simple shape on an eraser and cut away what should not print.
l2c: Ink it and print it on paper so the shape is recognizable.
l3c: If the first print is muddy, clean the stamp and print a clearer one.
safety: Cut away from your hand. This is not linocut with sharp gouges.

name: Make a pinch pot
description: Form a small pot from a ball of clay that can sit without collapsing.
l1c: Pinch a ball of clay into a hollow that sits flat.
l2c: Show a wall that is not paper-thin in one spot and thick in another, as far as you can.
l3c: Set it aside to dry as the clay's own note says, and say you are not firing it.
l3d: You can stop before a kiln.
safety: Air-dry or classroom clay only. No kiln in this skill. Wash your hands.

name: Join two pieces of clay
description: Join a handle or a coil to a clay body so it holds when leather-hard.
l1c: Roughen both surfaces and use slip or water as your clay guide says.
l2c: Press the pieces together and smooth the seam.
l3c: When the clay is firmer, look at the seam and press or note a crack.
safety: No kiln. A glue joint in wood is a different skill.

name: Weave a paper mat
description: Weave paper strips into a mat that holds when you pick it up.
l1c: Lay strips one way and fix the ends so they stay parallel.
l2c: Weave the other strips over and under, alternating the next row.
l3c: Fold or tape the edge so a strip does not fall out when you lift the mat.
safety: Mind paper cuts. A cord braid is a different skill.

name: Fold a paper envelope
description: Fold an envelope that closes and holds a card.
l1c: Fold a sheet so three sides can hold a card.
l2c: Tuck or stick the flap so the card stays in when you turn it over.
l3c: Write a practice address on it, or say you will use a real envelope for the post.
l3d: You can see the limit of a homemade envelope.
safety: A posted letter uses the postal service's rules. Addressing a real envelope is a different skill.

name: Sew a visible patch
description: Sew a patch over a small hole so the patch covers the damage.
l1c: Pin a patch that extends past the hole on every side.
l2c: Sew around the patch and fasten the thread.
l3c: Look at the back and restitch a gap, or say the hole is still open and you are not done.
safety: A split seam is a different skill. Do not patch load-bearing gear.

name: Darn a small hole
description: Stitch across a small hole in knit fabric so it does not gape.
l1c: Sew threads across a small hole, anchored in sound fabric.
l2c: Weave the other direction through those threads.
l3c: Tug gently and show that the darn stays, or mark it as too weak to wear.
safety: Do not darn something that must hold a person. Mind the needle.

name: Fold a one-page zine
description: Fold one sheet into a small booklet with a cover and an order.
l1c: Fold one sheet into a booklet and number the pages in reading order.
l2c: Add a title and one idea that continues across the pages.
l3c: Give it to someone and ask which page they read after the cover.
safety: A blank notebook is a different skill. Use images you may use.

name: Take a soundwalk
description: Walk a short way and note the sounds without recording anyone's private talk.
l1c: Walk a short route and write three sounds you heard.
l1d: You can listen on a walk.
l2c: Say which sound was near, which was far, and which you could not place.
l3c: If you heard a private conversation, do not write the words, and say you left them out.
safety: Do not record people. Watch the path while you listen.

name: Name the sounds in a room
description: List the sounds in a room and mark one you cannot identify.
l1c: Sit still and list the sounds you hear.
l2c: Point to the source of one sound, such as a vent or a clock.
l2d: You can tie a sound to a source.
l3c: Mark one sound you will not name, because you cannot find the source.
l3d: You can leave a sound unknown.
safety: None.

name: Describe a quiet moment
description: Describe a moment that is quiet, including the small sounds that remain.
l1c: Find a quieter spot and say what got softer.
l2c: Name one sound that is still there.
l3c: Say whether the spot is quiet enough for the task you had in mind, such as reading aloud.
l3d: You can judge a spot for a task.
safety: None.

name: Notice when people talk over each other
description: In a conversation you are part of, notice an overlap and make room.
l1c: Notice when two people speak at once, including yourself.
l2c: If you were one of them, stop and let the other person finish.
l3c: Ask the person who was cut off to finish, if they want to.
safety: Letting everyone speak once is a different skill. Do not force a reply.

name: Take notes for someone you accompany
description: Go with someone who asked you to, and write only what they want recorded.
l1c: Before you go, agree what you will write and what you will not.
l1d: You can take a bounded job.
l2c: Write the points they indicate, in their words as far as you can.
l3c: Give them the notes and delete or leave out anything they say is too private.
safety: You are not an advocate or a clinician. Do not give advice. Do not share the notes.

name: Prepare a place for a guest to sleep
description: Prepare a sleeping place with a clear surface, a light, and a way to ask for what is missing.
l1c: Clear a surface for their bag and make the bed with clean linen if you have it.
l1d: You can prepare the bed space.
l2c: Show the light, the toilet, and where water is.
l3c: Ask what they still need and either provide it or say you cannot.
l3d: You can finish with their answer.
safety: Making a bed is a different skill. Do not offer medicine.

name: Agree how you will check in
description: Agree with someone when you will contact them and what silence means.
l1c: Propose a time and a channel.
l2c: Agree what you will do if they do not answer.
l3c: Send the check-in at the time, and follow the agreed step if there is no answer.
safety: This is not surveillance. Either person can cancel it.

name: Read steps while someone else works
description: Read instructions while another person does the task, and stop when they say stop.
l1c: Read one step, then wait until they finish it.
l2c: Repeat a step without adding advice they did not ask for.
l2d: You can stick to the text.
l3c: Stop reading when they take over or when the instruction is unclear, and say which.
safety: Do not read steps for electrical, gas, or medical work. Writing instructions is a different skill.

name: Wait without filling the silence
description: Leave a silence so the other person can speak, instead of jumping in.
l1c: After they stop, wait before you speak.
l2c: If they continue, do not talk over the new sentence.
l2d: You can let the silence work.
l3c: If they do not continue, ask whether they want a question or quiet, and follow the answer.
l3d: You can check instead of assuming.
safety: Active listening is a different skill.

name: Pass an object so it can be taken
description: Pass an object handle-first, or say how the other person should take it.
l1c: Hold a tool or a cup so the other person can take the safe part.
l2c: Do not let go until they have it, or until they refuse.
l3c: If the object is hot, wet, or sharp, say so before you pass it.
l3d: You can warn before the handoff.
safety: Do not pass knives in a crowd. Do not pass anything hot without the warning.

name: Offer guidance beside you
description: Offer your arm as a guide, describe the next change, and stop when the person lets go.
l1c: Offer your arm and wait until they take it or decline.
l2c: Before a turn, a curb, or a door, say what is coming.
l3c: If they let go or say stop, stop guiding and ask what they want next.
safety: This is not an orientation-and-mobility qualification. Do not grab a person or their cane.

name: Stay in the role you were given
description: At an appointment or a meeting, do only the task the person asked of you.
l1c: Before you go in, restate the task they gave you.
l2c: During the meeting, decline a task they did not ask for, or ask them before you take it.
l3c: Afterward, ask what they want remembered, and do not tell others their business.
safety: You are not their representative unless they said so. Do not share health or legal details.

name: Read a public notice
description: Read a public notice and say what it announces, who it is from, and the date.
l1c: Point to what is announced, who published it, and the date, or say which is missing.
l2c: Say who would need to act, according to the notice.
l3c: Point to the contact or the deadline, or say the notice does not give one.
l3d: You can find the next step.
safety: Plain-language rewriting is a different skill. Do not give legal advice.

name: Find who runs a local service
description: Find the office responsible for a local service, from a page or a sign you can show.
l1c: Write the service you mean, such as the library or the park.
l2c: Find a page or a sign that names the office, and save the name.
l2d: You can find a named office.
l3c: Find one official way to ask a question, or say you could not.
l3d: You can stop at a real contact path.
safety: Use an official page or a sign on the building. Do not use a link from an unexpected message.

name: Read what a public question would change
description: Read a ballot or consultation question and say what it says would change, without choosing a side.
l1c: Read the question aloud as it is written.
l2c: In your own words, say what the text says would change if it passed, and point to the sentence.
l3c: Say one thing the text does not tell you, and do not add a recommendation.
l3d: You can stop before advising a vote.
safety: This is reading, not campaigning and not legal advice.

name: Find a public meeting
description: Find the time and place of a public meeting from an official notice.
l1c: Find a notice that names a meeting.
l2c: Write the time and the place, including whether it is online.
l3c: Check that the date has not passed, or say the notice is old.
l3d: You can reject a stale notice.
safety: Use the official notice. Attendance rules are whatever the notice says.

name: Write a factual note to a local service
description: Write to a library, council, or similar service about a fact you saw, and ask one question.
l1c: Write what you saw, where, and when.
l2c: Add one question that the fact makes relevant.
l2d: You can ask from the fact.
l3c: Remove a sentence that insults or that asks for something you cannot justify, and send or save the note.
l3d: You can keep the note factual.
safety: Do not include anyone's private data. This is not a legal filing.

name: Plan a visit from the opening hours
description: Use published opening hours to choose a time you can actually arrive.
l1c: Find the hours for the day you want, including a holiday note if it is there.
l2c: Choose a time inside those hours, with room to get there.
l2d: You can pick a real time.
l3c: Say what you will do if you arrive and it is unexpectedly closed.
safety: A transit timetable is a different skill.

name: Find an accessible entrance on a sign
description: Use a sign or a map at a building to find the entrance that avoids steps.
l1c: Find the access symbol or the words that point to the entrance.
l2c: Go there, or say the sign runs out.
l3c: If the entrance is locked or missing, note that and the time.
l3d: You can report a failed entrance.
safety: Do not force a door. Finding a step-free route is the same family; this one starts from a building's own sign.

name: Keep a confirmation
description: Save a confirmation so you can show the time and the reference later.
l1c: Point to the date and the reference on a confirmation you received.
l1d: You can see what to keep.
l2c: Put it where you can find it, without posting it publicly.
l3c: Later, show the date and reference, and cover any extra personal numbers.
safety: A reservation skill already exists. This one is about keeping the proof.

name: Steady a wobble you can see
description: Stop a small wobble with a pad or by moving the object, and say if the frame is the problem.
l1c: Rock the object and point to the foot that leaves the floor.
l2c: Add a pad or move the object so it sits quieter.
l3c: If the frame is cracked or the wobble remains, say you will not force it.
safety: Do not stand on the object. Structural repair is not this skill.

name: Tighten a screw you can see
description: Tighten one visible screw on furniture until it sits, and stop if it spins.
l1c: Choose a driver that fits the screw head.
l2c: Turn it until it is snug, and show that the part sits closer.
l3c: If the screw spins or the hole is stripped, stop and say so.
l3d: You can abandon a bad hole.
safety: Do not open an electrical cover. Do not force a screw you cannot see.

name: Silence a hinge as the label says
description: Quiet a hinge using only a product whose label says it can be used on a hinge.
l1c: Show the label that names hinges or moving metal, and the amount.
l1d: You can start from the label.
l2c: Apply only that amount and wipe the excess.
l3c: Open the door and say whether the squeak is quieter, and stop if the door will not latch.
l3d: You can check the door still closes.
safety: Do not mix products. Do not remove the door from a fire closer.

name: Set a clock after it lost time
description: Set a clock to a time source you can name, including the date if it shows one.
l1c: Name the time source you will trust, such as an official clock.
l2c: Set the clock, including the date if it drifted.
l3c: If it has an alarm you rely on, show that the alarm time is still the one you want.
l3d: You can check the alarm survived.
safety: Do not open the mains. A time-zone conversion is a different skill.

name: Test a bicycle brake
description: Squeeze a brake and say whether the wheel stops, without adjusting a cable.
l1c: With the bike still, lift the wheel and spin it.
l2c: Squeeze the lever and say whether the wheel stops promptly.
l3c: If it does not stop the wheel, say you will not ride it, and do not adjust the cable in this skill.
safety: Test off the road. Cable and hydraulic work are not included. Inflating a tire is a different skill.

name: Replace a shoelace
description: Thread a new lace so both shoes match and the ends do not pull out.
l1c: Remove one lace and keep the path it used.
l2c: Thread a new lace along that path so the ends come out even.
l3c: Do the second shoe the same way, or say you are leaving it until you have a second lace.
l3d: You can keep a pair consistent.
safety: None.

name: Rehang a curtain ring
description: Put a curtain ring back on its rod so the curtain hangs with the others.
l1c: Find the missing ring and the place it left.
l2c: Put the ring on the rod and the curtain on the ring.
l3c: Slide the curtain and say whether the rings move, and stop if the rod comes down.
safety: Do not stand on a wobbly chair. If you cannot reach safely, stop.

name: Fit a battery the right way
description: Match a battery to the marks in a device and seat the cover.
l1c: Point to the plus and minus marks in the compartment and on the battery.
l2c: Insert the battery so the marks agree, and close the cover.
l3c: Turn the device on, or say it still does not work and you will not force another battery in.
l3d: You can stop if it fails.
safety: Do not open a sealed battery. Do not mix old and new cells if the device says not to.

name: Make a legend
description: Add a legend so someone else can read the marks on your sketch.
l1c: List each mark you used and what it means.
l2n: Put the legend on the page
l2c: Place the legend where it is not mistaken for part of the drawing.
l3c: Ask someone to say what one mark means, using only the legend.
safety: A rough floor plan is a different skill. This one explains the marks.

name: Design a one-page sign
description: Make a sign with one message that a person can read at a glance.
l1c: Write the one thing the sign must say, in a few words.
l2c: Letter it large, with empty space around the words.
l3c: Show it briefly to someone and ask what it said. Fix it if they miss the message.
safety: Checking contrast in place is a different skill. Do not post the sign where you are not allowed.

name: Test a form with a person
description: Watch one person fill a form you made or chose, and fix one confusion.
l1c: Give them the form and do not explain the fields while they try.
l2c: Write the field where they stop or ask a question.
l2d: You can see a stuck field.
l3c: Rewrite the label of that field and say what was unclear.
safety: Filling a form yourself is a different skill. Do not collect real identity numbers in the test.

name: Order steps on a card
description: Put steps on a card in the order a person must do them.
l1c: Write the steps of a safe everyday task you know.
l2c: Number them so a later step does not require an earlier one you have not listed.
l3c: Have someone point to a missing step, and add it or say it belongs elsewhere.
safety: Do not write cards for electrical, gas, or medical tasks. Watching someone follow your steps is a different skill.

name: Choose a size people can read
description: Set type or lettering large enough for the reader you have in mind.
l1c: Say who will read it and from how far.
l2c: Make two sizes and ask that reader, or someone standing in for them, which they can read.
l3c: Use the size they could read, and say if a longer text still will not fit.
l3d: You can choose and note the limit.
safety: Lettering a single word by hand is a different skill.

name: Keep a color code
description: Use colors to mean the same things across one page.
l1c: Write what each color means before you use it.
l2c: Use the colors only for those meanings on the page.
l2d: You can stick to the code.
l3c: Find one place the color could be misread, and change it or add a word.
safety: Mixing a paint color is a different skill. Do not rely on color alone.

name: Leave room for a note
description: Lay out a page so a person can write a note on it.
l1c: Leave a blank space and label what should be written there.
l2c: Write a typical note in the space and see whether it fits.
l3c: If it does not fit, enlarge the space or shorten the prompt.
safety: Digital page layout is a different skill.

name: Sketch a screen on paper
description: Sketch a screen on paper and say what each part does before any software.
l1c: Draw the main regions of one screen and label them.
l2c: Point to the one action the screen is for.
l3c: Tell a person what they would tap or read first, and change a label they do not understand.
l3d: You can test the paper screen.
safety: Publishing a real layout is a different skill. Do not collect passwords on the sketch.

name: Note a track without guessing the animal
description: Record a track you see and leave it unnamed if you are not sure.
l1c: Describe the shape, the size relative to your hand, and where you found it.
l2c: Look for another print and say whether the direction is clear.
l2d: You can look for a line of prints.
l3c: If you are not sure of the animal, write unknown, and do not pick a likely species.
l3d: You can leave a track unnamed.
safety: Do not follow an animal. Wildlife field notes are a different skill. Do not touch droppings.

name: Watch an insect on a flower
description: Watch one insect visit a flower and write what it did.
l1c: Watch one insect for a short time and write what it did on the flower.
l2c: Describe the flower well enough to find a similar one, without requiring a species name.
l3n: Say what you did not see
l3c: Write one thing you did not see, such as where the insect went next.
safety: Do not touch the insect. Do not disturb a nest. Naming plants is a different skill.

name: Compare two leaf edges
description: Compare the edges of two leaves and say how they differ.
l1c: Take two fallen leaves or look at two you do not pick, and lay the comparison out.
l1d: You can set up the comparison.
l2c: Say how the edges differ, using words such as smooth, toothed, or lobed.
l3c: Say you have not named the plants, unless a guide you can show confirms them.
l3d: You can stop before an identification.
safety: Do not pick a protected plant. Do not eat the leaves.

name: Notice a plant growing in a hard place
description: Notice a plant growing in a crack or a gutter and describe its spot.
l1c: Find a plant growing in a crack, a wall, or another hard spot.
l2c: Say what the spot is made of and whether the plant has light and water you can see.
l3c: Leave the plant where it is, and say why you are not pulling it.
safety: Do not pull plants from walls. Growing from seed is a different skill.

name: Tell damp ground from dry
description: Look at and feel the ground and say whether it is damp, and what you will not infer.
l1c: Look at the color and the sheen of the ground.
l2c: Touch the surface and say whether it is damp.
l3c: Say you cannot tell how deep the water goes, or whether it is safe to cross.
l3d: You can stop at the surface.
safety: Do not walk onto mud or ice to test it. Watering a pot is a different skill.

name: Split a word into parts
description: Split a long word into parts and say what each part does, using a dictionary when you need it.
l1c: Mark the parts of a long word you can justify.
l2c: Check one part in a dictionary and correct your split if needed.
l3c: Use the word in a sentence that would fail if you had the parts wrong.
safety: Looking up a whole word is a different skill.

name: Find the plain meaning of an idiom
description: Find what an idiom means in plain words, and the situation it came from if you know it.
l1c: Look up an idiom and write the plain meaning.
l2c: Use it in a sentence where it fits, or say the situation is wrong for it.
l3c: If you tell where the phrase came from, mark that as a story you sourced, or leave it out.
l3d: You can avoid a fake origin.
safety: Do not invent an etymology.

name: Notice word order
description: In a sentence you did not write, point to the word order that carries the meaning.
l1c: Point to who or what did the action, and the action, in someone else's sentence.
l2c: Say how the sentence would change if one phrase moved, without claiming a grammar certificate.
l2d: You can see that order matters.
l3c: Find a second sentence with a different order and say what the difference does.
safety: Foreign-language conversation is a different skill.

name: Keep a phrase and its situation
description: Save a phrase you heard, the situation, and whether you would use it.
l1c: Write the phrase and where you heard it.
l2c: Write who could say it and who it might offend or confuse.
l3c: Mark whether you will use it, and why.
safety: Writing in a language you are learning is a different skill. Do not record a private conversation.

name: Read a bilingual sign
description: Read a sign in two languages and say what matches and what you cannot check.
l1c: Read both versions as far as you can.
l2c: Say one part that clearly matches, such as a place name or a time.
l3c: Mark a part you cannot verify, and do not claim the translations are equal.
safety: Short-text translation is a different skill. This one does not produce a translation.

name: Apologize and offer a repair
description: Apologize for a specific act and offer a repair the other person can accept or refuse.
l1c: Say what you did, without adding their motive.
l2c: Offer one concrete repair.
l3c: If they refuse or want something else, accept that answer and do not insist.
safety: A clear refusal is a different skill. Do not apologize for a harm you do not understand; ask first.

name: Receive a compliment
description: Hear a compliment and respond without cancelling it.
l1c: Let the person finish the compliment.
l2c: Thank them without insulting the thing they praised.
l3c: If you want to know more, ask one question, or stop at the thanks.
l3d: You can choose whether to extend it.
safety: None.

name: Ask for a pause
description: Ask to pause a conversation and say when you can return.
l1c: Ask for a pause in one sentence.
l2c: Say when you will come back, or that you cannot name a time yet.
l3c: Return at that time, or send an update if you cannot.
safety: Conflict resolution is a different skill. You can pause without settling the issue.

name: Name a boundary for a topic
description: Say that a topic is off limits for you, and what you can talk about instead.
l1c: Say which topic you will not discuss.
l2c: Offer another topic, or say you are ending the conversation.
l2d: You can give a next step.
l3c: If they return to the closed topic, restate the boundary once, and stop if they continue.
safety: You do not owe a reason. Declining a request is a different skill.

name: Close a conversation
description: End a conversation so the other person knows it is ending.
l1c: Say that you need to stop, in a sentence.
l2c: Say the next step, or that there is none.
l3c: Leave or let them leave, without starting a new topic.
safety: None.

name: Congratulate a specific effort
description: Congratulate someone for a specific effort, not a vague trait.
l1c: Say the specific effort they made, in a sentence they would recognize.
l2c: Add why that effort mattered to the work or the people there.
l3c: Leave out a label about the kind of person they are, and send or say the note.
safety: A thank-you for a favor is a different skill.

name: Share a mistake so others can avoid it
description: Tell others about a mistake you made, the cause, and the check that would catch it.
l1c: Say what you did and what happened.
l2c: Name the check that would have caught it.
l2d: You can turn it into a check.
l3c: Tell it without blaming a person who is not there, and invite one question.
safety: A checklist from a miss is a different skill. Do not include private data.

name: Place a lamp for the work
description: Place a lamp so the work is lit and the glare is not in your eyes.
l1c: Aim a lamp at the work surface.
l2c: Move the lamp or the page until the bright spot is not in your eyes.
l3c: Ask someone whether they can see the work, and move the lamp if they cannot.
l3d: You can set light for more than yourself.
safety: Do not open the lamp. Keep cloth away from a hot bulb.

name: Reduce glare on a screen
description: Move a screen or a light so you can see the content.
l1c: Point to the reflection that hides the content.
l2c: Move the screen, the light, or your seat, and show that the content is easier to see.
l3c: If it is still hard to see, say what you would change next, or that you would stop.
l3d: You can admit a remaining limit.
safety: Do not open the device.

name: Clear a work surface
description: Clear a surface so the task has room, and put the cleared things where you can find them.
l1n: Remove what the task does not need
l1c: Take off the items the next task does not use.
l2c: Put those items in one place you can name.
l2d: You can avoid a second mess.
l3c: Start the task on the clear surface, and say if you still lack room.
safety: Do not throw away someone else's things.

name: Make a landing spot for essentials
description: Choose one spot for keys or a similar essential, and use it once.
l1c: Choose a spot near the way you leave, and tell the household if they share it.
l2c: Put the item there when you come in.
l3c: Next time you leave, find it there, or fix the spot if you did not.
safety: A list of important documents is a different skill. Do not hide a key outside.

name: Label a storage box
description: Label a box with what is inside and check the label by opening it later.
l1c: Write what is in the box, specific enough to search for.
l2c: Put the label where you can read it without opening the box.
l3c: Later, find one item using the label, and correct the label if the item is not there.
safety: None.

name: Carry a load close to you
description: Carry a moderate load close to your body and put it down if the path is unclear.
l1c: Pick up a box you can manage and hold it against your torso.
l1d: You can hold a load close.
l2c: Walk only where you can see the floor, and stop if you cannot.
l2d: You can keep a view of the path.
l3n: Put it down to open a door
l3c: Put the load down or set it aside to open a door, rather than forcing it.
safety: Do not carry more than you can put down safely. Do not carry up a ladder. Sharp pain means stop.

name: Lift a box with your legs
description: Lift a light box by bending your knees, and stop if the box is too heavy.
l1c: Stand close to the box, feet stable, and bend your knees rather than rounding to grab it.
l1d: You can set up a lift.
l2c: Lift it and hold it close. If it feels too heavy, put it back down.
l3c: Turn by moving your feet, not by twisting only your back, and set the box down.
safety: This is not a weightlifting program. Do not lift a person. Stop for sharp pain.

name: Keep a tally
description: Count events with a tally someone else can check.
l1c: Make one mark for one event, and say what counts as an event.
l2c: Group marks so a later reader can count them quickly, and total them.
l3c: Count the events again, or have someone else count the marks, and fix a mismatch.
safety: Keeping a game score is a different skill.

name: Estimate a crowd from a sample
description: Estimate how many people are in a space by counting a part, and show the arithmetic.
l1c: Count the people in one clearly bounded part of the space.
l2c: Say how many such parts fit in the space, and multiply.
l3c: Name one way the crowd is uneven, so the estimate could be off.
safety: Do not use this for a safety capacity you are not responsible for. Estimating then measuring is a different skill.

name: Check a sale price
description: Work out a sale price from the original and the discount, and compare it with the tag.
l1c: Point to the original price and the discount on a tag or a sign.
l2c: Compute the sale price and show the arithmetic.
l3c: Compare your result with the price charged, and say whether they match.
safety: Comparing unit prices is a different skill. This is not a loan comparison.

name: Divide a length into equal parts
description: Divide a length into equal parts and check by measuring.
l1c: Say how many equal parts you want.
l2c: Mark the parts on a strip or a line.
l3c: Measure the parts and adjust one mark that is off.
safety: A technical drawing is a different skill. Do not use a blade toward your hand.

name: Read a household thermometer
description: Read a room or outdoor thermometer, including the unit, and say what you will not infer.
l1c: Say the number and whether it is Celsius or Fahrenheit.
l2c: Read it again later and say whether it rose or fell.
l3c: Say this does not tell you whether a person has a fever or whether food is safe.
l3d: You can refuse a medical use.
safety: Do not use a clinical thermometer on someone else in this skill. Weather recording is broader and already exists.

name: Convert 12-hour and 24-hour time
description: Convert a time between 12-hour and 24-hour forms and check it.
l1c: Convert a time and say whether it is morning or evening.
l2c: Convert it back and show that you return to the start.
l3c: Write a meeting time in the form the other person uses.
l3d: You can use the form they need.
safety: A time-zone gap is a different skill.

name: Tell which date order a document uses
description: Say whether a document writes the day or the month first, using a date that makes it obvious.
l1c: Find a numeric date on a document.
l2c: Use a number greater than 12, or the document's own words, to say which order it uses.
l3c: Find or imagine a date such as 04/05 and say you cannot tell the order from that date alone.
l3d: You can refuse an ambiguous date.
safety: Do not enter a date into a form until the order is clear. Filling a form is a different skill.

name: Ask for a story and write it down
description: Ask one prepared question about a memory, write the answer, and check it with the teller.
l1c: Ask a question you prepared, and let the person answer.
l2c: Write the answer and mark anything you were unsure you heard.
l3c: Read it back and change what they say is wrong. Do not share it unless they agree.
safety: Genealogy research is a different skill. Do not record audio unless they agree. They may stop.

name: Put photographs in order
description: Put a few photographs in an order you can justify.
l1c: Look for dates, ages, or places on a small set of photos.
l2c: Put them in an order and say the clue for each step.
l3c: Leave one photo unordered if the clue is missing, and say so.
safety: Use photos you are allowed to handle. A caption skill is different.

name: Write what you know about an old photo
description: Write what you know about an old photo, separate from what you suppose.
l1c: Write only facts someone told you or that are written on the photo.
l1d: You can stick to the known.
l2c: If you add a guess, mark it as a guess.
l3c: Ask the person who keeps the photo to confirm one line, and correct it.
l3d: You can check with the keeper.
safety: Do not publish the photo. Writing a caption for a new image is a different skill.

name: Find the chorus of a song
description: Listen to a song and point to the part that returns.
l1c: Listen to a song you are allowed to play and note a part that comes back.
l2c: Play or sing the start of that part when it returns.
l3c: Say one thing that is different the second time, or that it is the same.
safety: Learning a tune by ear is a different skill. Keep the volume safe.

name: Clap the stresses of a word
description: Clap the stressed beats of a word or a short line.
l1c: Clap the louder beat of a word with more than one beat.
l2c: Clap the stresses of a short line you can see.
l3c: Say how the line would sound if the stress moved, and clap that version once.
l3d: You can hear a moved stress.
safety: Clapping a written rhythm is a different skill.

name: Find a rhyme
description: Find the rhymes in a short poem and say where the pattern breaks.
l1c: Mark the line endings that rhyme.
l2c: Say which lines rhyme with which.
l3c: Point to a line that does not fit the pattern, or say the pattern holds.
safety: None.

name: Mirror a gesture
description: Mirror a partner's slow gesture, and notice when you add a move they did not make.
l1c: Mirror a slow gesture as they do it.
l2c: Keep mirroring for a short run without adding a move.
l3c: Name one move you added or missed, and try that moment again.
safety: Stop if either person is uncomfortable. This is not mockery.

name: Build a den that leaves the exit clear
description: Build a temporary den from chairs and cloth that does not block the way out.
l1c: Point to the door and build so the path to it stays open.
l2c: Arrange cloth and chairs so the den stands when you are inside.
l3c: Take it down and put the chairs back.
safety: Do not use candles. Do not block a door. A tent outdoors is a different skill.

name: Write a plant-care note for someone else
description: Write how to care for one plant while you are away, including when not to water.
l1c: Write how you decide whether the soil is dry.
l2c: Write what they should not do, such as watering every day regardless.
l3c: Write how they should tell you if the plant wilts.
l3d: You can leave a path for bad news.
safety: Watering by checking the soil is your own skill. This one is the note. Do not prescribe pesticides.

name: Share a place pin
description: Send a place pin and check that the other person opened the same place.
l1c: Send a pin or a map link for a place you both may visit.
l2c: Ask them to read back the place name.
l3c: If they see the wrong place, send a landmark or a corrected pin.
safety: Do not share a home address in a public post. A transit map is a different skill.

name: Use guide words in a dictionary
description: Use the guide words on a dictionary page to find a word.
l1c: Read the two guide words on a page and say which words would belong there.
l2c: Open the right page for a word you chose and point to the entry.
l3n: Say you are on the wrong page
l3c: If the word is not there, say whether to go forward or back, and find it.
safety: Looking up a meaning and using it is a different skill.

name: Follow a cross-reference
description: Follow a see-also reference and say whether it answered your question.
l1c: Point to a see-also or a footnote marker.
l2c: Go to the place it names.
l3c: Say whether the new place answered the question, or that you need another source.
safety: Tracing a number to a source is a different skill.

name: Credit an image you may use
description: Use an image only if its terms allow, and write the credit those terms ask for.
l1c: Find the license or the statement that says you may use the image.
l2c: Write the credit the terms ask for, next to the image.
l3c: Set aside one image whose terms you cannot find, and do not use it.
l3d: You can refuse a missing license.
safety: Do not strip a watermark. Giving credit for an idea is a different skill.

name: Export a file someone can open
description: Save a file in a form another person can open, and check with them.
l1c: Ask which kind of file they can open.
l2c: Export or save in that form and send it.
l3c: Ask them to open it and resend in another form if they cannot.
safety: Organizing your own files is a different skill. Do not send a file you are not allowed to share.

name: Summarize a written thread
description: Summarize a written thread so a new reader knows the decision and the open question.
l1c: Read the thread and write any decision it contains.
l2c: Write the question that is still open, or say there is none.
l3c: Ask one participant if the summary missed a decision, and fix it if it did.
safety: Summarizing speech is a different skill. Do not forward a private thread.

name: Unpack an archive and find the file
description: Open a compressed archive and find the file you were sent, without running a program you did not expect.
l1c: Open a zip or similar archive you were expecting.
l2c: Find the named file inside and open that file.
l3c: If you see a program you were not told about, do not run it, and say so.
l3d: You can refuse an unexpected program.
safety: Recognizing a suspicious message is a different skill. Open only files you expected from someone you asked.

name: Check a link before you share it
description: Open a link yourself and say what the page is before you send it on.
l1c: Open the link and read the title of the page.
l2c: Write one sentence on what the page actually is.
l3c: Share it only if it matches what you meant to send, and say so if you stop.
l3d: You can withhold a bad link.
safety: Do not log in from a link you did not expect. Do not enter a password to check a link.

name: Make a paper puppet stage
description: Make a small stage from a box so a puppet can appear and leave.
l1c: Cut an opening in a box that is big enough for the puppet.
l2c: Bring a puppet into the opening and take it out.
l3c: Show that you can still reach the puppet and that the box is not closing anyone in.
l3d: You can keep the play safe.
safety: Cut away from your hand. Moving the puppet is a different skill.

name: Sort recycling by the sign in front of you
description: Sort items using the categories on the bin or the local sign, not a general rule.
l1c: Read the categories on the bins where you are.
l1d: You can read the local sign.
l2c: Put each item in a named category, or set it aside if it is not listed.
l3c: Show one item you did not put in, and the reason the sign does not list it.
safety: Do not wash chemicals into a bin. Local rules differ. A schedule you remember is not this skill.

name: Use a window as a light source
description: Place work near a window and say when the daylight is not enough.
l1c: Place the work where daylight falls on it.
l2c: Turn the work if you are in your own shadow.
l2d: You can get out of your shadow.
l3c: If the daylight fades, add a lamp or stop, and say which.
l3d: You can respond when daylight fails.
safety: Placing a lamp is a different skill. Do not stand on the sill.

name: Agree a spot for a shared tool
description: Agree where a shared tool lives, and put it back once.
l1c: Propose a spot the people who use the tool can reach.
l1d: You can propose a home for the tool.
l2c: Agree the spot with at least one other user.
l3c: Use the tool and put it back, or say you left it out and then return it.
safety: Do not agree a spot for a dangerous tool you are not trained to store.

name: Draw the route of a story
description: Draw where a story you heard or read moved, and mark a place you do not know.
l1c: List the places the story names, in order.
l2c: Sketch a path that connects the places you can locate.
l3c: Mark a place you cannot locate, and do not invent a spot for it.
l3d: You can leave a gap on the map.
safety: A city transit map is a different skill. Use only stories you may retell.

name: Listen for the downbeat
description: Point to the strong beat in a piece of music you can hear.
l1c: Tap only the beat that feels like the start of the bar.
l2c: Count along for a few bars and say where you lost it if you did.
l2d: You can stay with the downbeat.
l3c: Come back in after a pause in your tapping and meet the next strong beat.
safety: Keeping a steady beat yourself is a different skill. Keep the volume safe.

name: Name an instrument you can hear
description: Name one instrument in a recording, and say if a second sound is unknown.
l1c: Point to one sound and name the instrument if you know it.
l2c: Check the liner note, the credit, or a second listen, and correct the name if needed.
l3c: Leave a second sound unnamed if you cannot tell, and say so.
safety: Tuning a string is a different skill.

name: Plan a quiet hour for a shared space
description: Agree one quiet hour in a shared space and keep it.
l1c: Propose an hour and the space it covers.
l2c: Agree it with the other person, including one exception they need.
l3c: Keep the hour, or if you break it, say so and agree the next one.
l3d: You can live with the agreement.
safety: A quiet-hours house rule already exists as a broader agreement. This one is a single named hour.

name: Return a borrowed thing
description: Return something you borrowed in the condition you agreed, and say if it changed.
l1c: When you borrow it, note one fact about its condition.
l2c: Return it by the time you agreed.
l3c: If it changed, say how, and ask what they want done.
safety: Do not hide damage. Agreeing a trade is a different skill.

name: Set a rule for a shared playlist
description: Agree how a shared playlist works, then add one track that follows the rule.
l1c: Write who may add tracks and what kind of track fits.
l2c: Add one track that fits, with the title and the artist.
l3c: If someone adds a track that breaks the rule, ask before you remove it, or leave it and note the break.
safety: Do not upload music you may not share. A chorus-finding skill is different.

name: Mark a walk for someone else
description: Mark a short walk you know so another person can follow your notes.
l1c: Write the turns of a short walk, with one landmark each.
l2c: Add about how long it took you, and say it is your pace.
l3n: Let them use it or correct it
l3c: Ask them to follow it, or walk it from the notes yourself a day later, and fix one unclear turn.
safety: Planning a walk with a turn-around time is a different skill. Stay on paths you already know are allowed.

name: Notice a repeated word
description: Notice a word a speaker or a page repeats, and say what job it might be doing.
l1c: Mark each time a chosen word appears in a short text or a short talk you may use.
l2c: Say whether the repeat emphasizes, organizes, or just fills, and mark your view as a reading.
l3c: Point to two appearances that do different work, or say they do the same work.
safety: None.

name: Build a tiny paper model of a room
description: Fold a tiny model of a room you are in, with the door in the right wall.
l1c: Fold a small open box for the room.
l2c: Mark the door on the wall that matches the real room.
l3c: Add one piece of furniture in the right relationship to the door.
safety: A rough floor plan is a different skill. This model is not to scale and not for building work.

name: Test a chair before you use it as a step
description: Decide not to stand on a chair that rocks, and choose a safer way to reach.
l1c: Rock the chair on the floor and say whether all feet sit.
l2c: If it rocks or is soft, say you will not stand on it.
l3c: Ask for a proper step, leave the object, or wait, and say which you chose.
l3d: You can choose a safer reach.
safety: Do not stand on the chair in this skill. Ladder use is not included.

name: Read the care line on a tool
description: Read the one-line care note on a tool and do only that, or say you will not.
l1c: Find the maker's short care note on the tool or its card.
l2c: Do the note, such as wipe dry or store closed, and nothing more.
l3c: If there is no note and you do not know the care, do not invent a lubricant or a cleaner.
safety: Power tools, blades, and electrical tools are out of this skill. Follow the note only when it is ordinary care.

name: Point out a blocked exit
description: If you see an exit blocked, tell the person responsible and leave the fixing to them.
l1c: Point to what is blocking the exit, from a safe place.
l2c: Tell a staff member or a host what is blocking it.
l3c: Do not move a heavy or unknown object, and say why you left it.
l3d: You can stop at the report.
safety: In an alarm, follow the exit signs and the staff. Do not investigate a fire. This is not fire training.

name: Choose a seat you can leave
description: Choose a seat you can leave without climbing over people, when you have a choice.
l1c: Look at the path from a free seat to the aisle.
l2c: Sit in a seat with a clear path, or say there is no such seat and you will stand or wait.
l3c: Leave by that path when you need to, without a new disturbance you could avoid.
safety: Follow staff instructions. Do not block an exit with bags.

name: Ask where to start in a gallery
description: Ask a guard or a desk where to start, and follow or adapt their answer.
l1c: Ask where a first-time visitor should start.
l2c: Go to the place they name, or say why you are choosing a different start.
l3c: Thank them and do not keep them from other visitors.
safety: Follow the gallery rules they give you.

name: Notice a label you cannot read
description: When a label is in a language you do not read, say so and find another way to the fact you need.
l1c: Say which label you cannot read.
l2c: Use a symbol, a number, or a picture on the same object.
l3c: Ask someone who reads it, or stop rather than guess the warning.
safety: Do not ignore a warning symbol you do not understand. Translation of a text is a different skill.

name: Make a rubbing of a texture
description: Make a rubbing of a texture you are allowed to touch.
l1c: Choose a texture you are allowed to touch, not a fragile object.
l2c: Hold paper still and rub until the texture shows.
l3c: Write what the surface was and where, so the rubbing is a record.
safety: Do not rub a museum object, a gravestone if the place forbids it, or paint that might contain lead.

name: Stack a stable pile
description: Stack books or boxes so the pile is smaller at the top and does not lean.
l1c: Put the largest or heaviest at the bottom.
l2c: Add items only while the pile does not lean, and stop when it does.
l3c: Take the pile down from the top.
safety: Do not stack above your head. Do not climb the pile.

name: Match a lid to its container
description: Match lids to containers and set aside one that does not fit.
l1c: Find the lid that fits one container and close it.
l2c: Match a small set and leave no lid forced on.
l3c: Set aside a lid or a container that has no partner, and label it or say it is spare.
l3d: You can refuse a bad fit.
safety: Do not force glass. Food storage safety is a different skill.

name: Coil a cable without a kink
description: Coil a cable so it lies in loops and uncoils without a knot.
l1c: Coil the cable into loops of similar size.
l2c: Fasten the coil with a strap or the cable's own end so it stays.
l3c: Uncoil it and show that it does not come out in a knot.
safety: Unplug the cable first if it is powered. Do not open a device. Do not coil a cable that is hot.

name: Match pairs from a wash
description: Match pairs from a wash and set aside the items that have no partner.
l1c: Find two items that belong together and say the clue.
l2c: Match the rest and put singles in one place.
l3c: Say whether a single waits for its partner or is done, and why.
safety: Washing by the label is a different skill.

name: Lay out tools for a task
description: Lay out only the tools a task needs, in the order you will use them.
l1c: List the tools the task needs before you fetch extras.
l2c: Put them in the order you will use them, with handles toward you.
l3n: Put away what you did not use
l3c: Put away a tool you did not use, and say why it was extra.
safety: Do not lay out power tools or blades for a task you are not doing. Passing an object is a different skill.

name: Read a size chart
description: Read a size chart and say which size matches a measurement you have.
l1c: Point to the body measurement the chart uses.
l1d: You can see what the chart measures.
l2c: Match a measurement you took to a size, and show the row.
l3c: If you are between sizes, say so, and do not claim the garment will fit.
safety: Measure over clothes only if the chart says to. This is not tailoring.

name: Follow a folding diagram
description: Follow a folding diagram one picture at a time and undo a wrong fold.
l1c: Make the first fold so your paper matches the first picture.
l2c: Follow the next pictures in order until the object is done or you are stuck.
l3c: If a fold is wrong, unfold to the last picture that matched, and say which picture.
safety: A paper box and an envelope are results. This skill is reading the diagram. Mind paper edges.

name: Trace a shape and cut it out
description: Trace a shape and cut it out so the line is still visible or just gone, as you intended.
l1c: Trace a shape you are allowed to copy onto paper.
l2c: Cut along the line you traced, keeping the shape in one piece.
l3c: Lay the cut on the original and say where you left the line.
safety: Cut away from your hand. Do not trace a work you may not copy for publication.

name: Make a card that stands
description: Fold a card that stands up and carries one message.
l1c: Fold a card so it stands on a table.
l2c: Put one message on the front or the inside, where the reader will see it.
l3c: Open and close it, and fix a fold that makes it fall.
safety: A specific thank-you is a different skill. This one is the card as an object.

name: Set a blanket out of the path
description: Set a blanket where people can still pass, and pack it up.
l1c: Choose a spot that is not on a path or in front of an exit.
l2c: Set the blanket and keep bags on it.
l3c: Pack everything you brought and look once for anything left.
l3d: You can leave the place clear.
safety: A packed meal is a different skill. Do not block a path. Follow the place's rules.

name: Count a collection you own
description: Count a small collection and write the number so you can check it later.
l1c: Count the items once and write the number and the date.
l2c: Group them so a second count is easier, and count again.
l3c: If the two counts differ, look for the missing or extra item and write what you find.
safety: This is not an inventory of valuables for insurance. A tally of events is a different skill.

name: Describe a dance you watched
description: Describe a dance you watched by naming one movement and one change, without claiming you can dance it.
l1c: Name one movement you saw, in ordinary words.
l2c: Say what changed when the music or the pattern changed.
l3c: Say you are not teaching the dance, and do not demonstrate a step you cannot do safely.
l3d: You can keep the role of a watcher.
safety: Dance technique skills already exist. This one is watching. Do not record performers against the rules.

name: Clap along and stop when you lose it
description: Clap along with music and stop when you are no longer with it, then say where you lost it.
l1c: Clap with a recording for a short stretch.
l2c: Stop when you notice you are off, instead of hiding it.
l3c: Say or replay the moment you lost the beat.
safety: Leading a group clap is a different skill. Protect your ears.

name: Choose a book by its blurb and check the opening
description: Choose a book from the blurb, then check the opening and say if the blurb matched.
l1c: Read the blurb and say what you expect the book to be.
l2c: Read the opening page before you decide the book matches the blurb.
l3c: Say one way the opening matches or breaks the blurb.
safety: Finding a book in a catalog is a different skill.

name: Mark a page you will return to
description: Mark a page with a note that tells your later self why to return.
l1c: Mark a page you mean to revisit.
l2c: Write a few words on why, specific enough to understand later.
l3c: Return later, use the note, and rewrite it if it did not help.
safety: Annotating a text is a different skill. Mark only a copy you may mark.

name: Explain why a joke worked
description: Say why a joke you heard worked, without repeating a joke that targets a person in the room.
l1c: Point to the moment the meaning turned.
l2c: Say what the listener had to assume before the turn.
l3c: If the joke needs a private fact about someone present, do not retell it, and say you are leaving it.
safety: Telling a story is a different skill.

name: Spot a repeated instruction
description: In a set of instructions, find a step that is said twice and might conflict.
l1c: Read a short set of instructions you are allowed to study.
l2c: Find two sentences that tell you to do the same thing, or say there is no repeat.
l3c: If they differ, say how, and which one you would ask about before doing the task.
l3d: You can stop before a conflict.
safety: Do not perform a dangerous instruction to test it.

name: Make a checklist someone else can tick
description: Write a checklist another person can tick without asking what the boxes mean.
l1c: Write checks that have a visible done state.
l2c: Ask someone to tick one item and see if they do the thing or only tick the box.
l2d: You can see a hollow tick.
l3c: Rewrite a line that was unclear so the action is visible.
safety: A checklist born from your own miss is a different skill. No dangerous tasks.

name: Agree a hand signal
description: Agree one hand signal and use it once at a distance where speech is hard.
l1c: Agree what one signal means before you separate.
l2c: Use it once, and have the other person do the agreed response.
