l3c: If they do not respond, stop relying on it and use a closer method.
l3d: You can abandon a failed signal.
safety: Do not use the signal in traffic or on water. Nonverbal communication as a general skill already exists; this one is one agreed signal.

name: Introduce a speaker in one sentence
description: Introduce a speaker with their name and why they are speaking, in one sentence.
l1c: Check how the speaker says their name and the topic.
l2c: Say one sentence with the name and the topic, then stop.
l3c: Stop talking and let them start, and correct the name at once if you misspoke.
safety: A personal introduction of yourself is a different skill. Do not add a private biography.

name: End a rehearsal on time
description: End a practice on the agreed time and say what the next practice will start with.
l1c: Say the end time at the start.
l2c: Stop at that time, even mid-run if you must.
l3c: Say the first thing the next practice will do.
safety: A timebox for a work task is a different skill.

name: Label a costume piece
description: Label a costume piece with the role and where it returns.
l1c: Attach a label with the role or the wearer.
l2c: Write where it is hung when it is off.
l2d: You can give it a home.
l3c: Put it back after use and check the label is still on.
safety: Do not label a person's body. Shared tools are a different agreement.

name: Call a cue for someone else
description: Give a cue at the agreed moment and not early.
l1n: Mark the cue in the text
l1c: Mark the word or action that triggers the cue.
l2c: Give the cue at that moment, loud enough for the person who needs it.
l3c: If you were early or late, mark the script and say how you will watch the next time.
safety: Taking a cue yourself is a different skill. No stage machinery.

name: Darken a room for a viewing
description: Darken a room enough to see a screen or a projection, and restore the light after.
l1c: Close blinds or switch off lights until the image is visible.
l2c: Leave enough light to see the way to the door, or say you cannot and stop.
l3c: Put the room back when the viewing ends.
safety: Do not cover a smoke alarm or a detector. Do not use candles.

name: Seat people so they can see
description: Arrange a few seats so each person can see the front, and move one that cannot.
l1c: Set seats facing the front.
l2c: Sit in the worst seat and say whether the front is visible.
l3c: Move a seat that fails, or say there is no better place.
safety: Do not block an exit. Choosing your own leavable seat is a different skill.

name: Write a content note
description: Write a short note that tells a reader what difficult thing is ahead, without describing it at length.
l1c: Write the topic in a few words.
l2c: Put the note before the material, where the reader can see it first.
l3c: Remove a sentence that retells the difficult part, and leave the short note.
l3d: You can keep the note from becoming the story.
safety: You choose whether to include the material at all. This is not a clinical warning.

name: Offer a written version of what you said
description: After you explain something aloud, offer the same points in writing.
l1c: Explain a small thing aloud.
l2c: Write the same points, not a new essay.
l2d: You can match the writing to the speech.
l3c: Ask whether the speech, the writing, or both was useful, and do not be hurt by the answer.
l3d: You can let them choose the form.
safety: Plain-language rewriting of a notice is a different skill.

name: Check a doorway with a tape
description: Measure a doorway and compare it with a width you were asked about.
l1c: Measure the clear width of a doorway with a tape, in the unit you were asked for.
l2c: Compare the number with the width you were given and say which is larger.
l3c: Note a threshold or a door swing that the number alone does not show.
l3d: You can add what the tape missed.
safety: This is not a building survey and not a promise that a wheelchair will pass. Do not alter the door.

name: Bundle cables and label them
description: Bundle cables you may touch and label what each one serves.
l1c: If a cable is safe to unplug, unplug it before you bundle, or leave it if you are not sure.
l1d: You can decide whether to unplug.
l2c: Bundle one cable and label the device it serves.
l3c: Follow the label to the device and correct the label if it is wrong.
safety: Do not unplug medical or safety equipment. Do not open a plug. Coiling without a kink is a different skill.

name: Look up a washing symbol you do not know
description: Look up one care symbol you do not know, from a chart you can show.
l1c: Copy or point to the symbol you do not know.
l2c: Find the same symbol on a care chart from the maker or a standards page you opened.
l3c: Say the action the chart gives, and do not wash the item in this skill.
l3d: You can stop at the meaning.
safety: Washing a load is a different skill. Use a chart you actually opened.

name: Make a timeline from stories you were told
description: Put stories you were told on a timeline and mark what has no date.
l1c: List events people told you, with the teller.
l2c: Place only the events that have a date or a clear order.
l3c: Leave undated events off the line and say they are unordered.
l3d: You can refuse a fake date.
safety: Placing a sourced historical event is a different skill. Do not publish a private family story.

name: Learn the order of a public ceremony
description: Learn the order of a public ceremony you may attend, and what a visitor is asked to do.
l1c: Find a program or a page from the place that lists the order.
l2c: Mark what a visitor is asked to do, such as stand, sit, or stay quiet.
l3c: If you are unsure whether visitors may join a moment, ask a host or stay seated, and say which you did.
l3d: You can wait rather than guess.
safety: Follow the host. Do not photograph if the place asks you not to. This is not religious instruction.

name: Choose a table you can work at
description: Choose a table for a quiet task and move if it does not work.
l1c: Before you settle, notice the noise and whether you can see your work.
l2c: Set up only the space you were given, without spreading into the aisle.
l2d: You can keep to your place.
l3c: If you cannot work, move or pack up, and say why.
l3d: You can leave a bad spot.
safety: Buy what the place requires or ask before you stay. Do not block a door.

name: Borrow a library item and note the due date
description: Borrow an item and record when it is due, then return or renew it.
l1c: Borrow an item on your own account.
l2c: Write the due date where you will see it.
l3c: Return it or renew it before the date, and keep the new receipt if you renew.
safety: Finding the book on the shelf is a different skill. Follow the library's rule.

name: Report something broken in a public place
description: Report a broken bench, a light, or a similar public thing to the office that handles it.
l1c: Write what is broken and where, with a landmark.
l2c: Send the note through the official path you found, not a random link.
l3c: Save any reference number, or say the path gave you none.
safety: Do not repair electrical or playground equipment yourself. Finding who runs a service is a different skill.

name: Change a plan from a weather icon
description: Read a forecast icon for the hour you care about and change one plan.
l1c: Read the icon and the hour it applies to.
l2c: Change one part of a plan, such as taking a cover or moving the time, because of that icon.
l2d: You can let the forecast change a plan.
l3c: Look outside at the time and say whether the icon matched, without claiming you forecast the day.
l3d: You can compare icon and sky.
safety: Recording and interpreting local weather is a different, broader skill. Do not go out in a warning you do not understand.

name: Keep a list of questions for a visit
description: Write questions before a visit and mark which ones got answers.
l1c: Write a few questions before you go.
l2c: During or after the visit, mark which questions were answered.
l3c: Leave one question open and say where you might ask it later.
l3d: You can keep an open question.
safety: Preparing one question for a guide is narrower. This one is the list.

name: Draw a diagram of a process you did
description: Draw a process as boxes and arrows, including one decision.
l1c: Draw the main steps of a process you did, in order.
l2c: Add one decision with two arrows.
l3c: Walk the diagram with someone and fix an arrow that points the wrong way.
safety: Documenting a process with photos is a different skill. No dangerous processes.

name: Separate a fact from a recommendation
description: In a short text, mark a fact and a recommendation.
l1c: Mark a sentence that reports something you could check.
l2c: Mark a sentence that tells the reader what to do or buy.
l3c: If the text has only one of those, say which is missing.
l3d: You can see a one-sided text.
safety: Evaluating claims and evidence is a broader skill. This one sorts two sentence types.

name: Make a symbol key for your notes
description: Choose a few symbols for your notes and use them the same way twice.
l1c: Write what a few symbols mean.
l2c: Use them in a real note.
l3c: Read the note later and say whether the symbols still make sense, then fix the key if not.
safety: A legend on a drawing is a different skill.

name: Host one quiet minute
description: Ask a group for one quiet minute and say what it was for.
l1c: Tell the group why you want one quiet minute.
l2c: Start it and end it, and stay quiet yourself.
l3c: Ask if anyone wants to say one thing they noticed, and accept silence.
safety: A soundwalk is a different skill. People may opt out.

name: Teach a hand position
description: Show a hand position for a craft or a piece of music and correct one visible difference.
l1c: Show the position on your own hand and name what matters.
l2c: Watch the other person try, and name one difference you can see.
l3c: Show the adjustment once, then let them decide whether it feels usable.
safety: Stop if they report pain. Tuning a string and textile skills are different.

name: Pack a shared bag from an agreed list
description: Pack a bag from a list two people agreed, and show the item you left out.
l1c: Agree a short list with the other person.
l2c: Pack those items and no surprise extra they did not ask for.
l3c: Show one thing you did not pack and why.
safety: Packing your own trip is a different skill. Do not pack another person's medicine.

name: Write the step-free note on an invitation
description: Add a step-free arrival note to an invitation, or say you do not know it yet.
l1c: Find the step-free entrance from the venue, or write that you do not know it.
l1d: You can look before you invite.
l2c: Put that sentence on the invitation if you know it.
l3c: Add a way for a guest to ask, if the note is missing or incomplete.
l3d: You can leave a way to ask.
safety: Hosting a meal is a different skill. Do not promise access you have not checked.

name: Practice saying a name you find difficult
description: Ask how to say a name, practice it, and use it once.
l1c: Ask the person to say their name and listen.
l2c: Repeat it and ask if it is close enough.
l3c: Use it once in the conversation, and apologize and retry if they correct you.
safety: Learning names in a group is a broader skill. Use the pronunciation they give you.

name: Decline a photo of yourself
description: Say no to a photo, or ask where it will go before you agree.
l1c: Before you agree, ask who will see the photo.
l2c: Agree, refuse, or agree only without your face, in a clear sentence.
l3c: If you refused and they ask again, repeat the no once and move away or change the subject.
safety: Taking a photo of a willing subject is a different skill.

name: Label a drawer of small parts
description: Sort a drawer of small parts into labeled groups.
l1c: Group similar small parts together before you label them.
l2c: Label each group with what it is, or with unknown.
l3c: Find one part from its label, and fix a label that failed.
safety: Do not sort loose batteries of unknown type into a hot place. Batteries in a device are a different skill.

name: Read how a queue works
description: Read how a queue works and take the right next step.
l1c: Read whether the queue uses a ticket, a line, or a call.
l2c: Take a ticket or join the line as the sign says.
l3c: If two signs conflict, ask a staff member instead of pushing ahead.
safety: Do not skip people. Leave a clear voicemail is a different skill.

name: Note the exit when you arrive
description: When you arrive in a public room, look for the exit sign and the path, without a drill.
l1c: Find the exit sign from your seat or the door.
l2c: See whether the path from you to that sign is open.
l3c: If you are with people who asked, tell them which way the sign points.
safety: Do not pull an alarm. Do not run a drill. If an alarm sounds, follow staff and the signs. Pointing out a blocked exit is a different skill.

name: Choose a meeting spot if you get separated
description: Agree a meeting spot before you enter a crowded place.
l1c: Name a spot you can both find, such as a specific door.
l2c: Say how long you will wait there before you use a phone.
l3c: If you do get separated, go there, or if you do not, say the plan stayed unused.
safety: Do not leave a child with a stranger as the plan. A transport-failure plan is a different skill.

name: Label a shared moving box
description: Label a shared box with the room and one fragile fact.
l1c: Write the room the box belongs to.
l2c: Add one handling note you mean, such as heavy or this way up, only if it is true.
l2d: You can add a true note.
l3c: Put the box in that room, or correct the label if the room was wrong.
safety: Do not lift a box that is too heavy. Lifting with your legs is a different skill.

name: Decide what not to photograph
description: Read a place's photo rule and leave one thing unphotographed.
l1c: Find the sign or the notice about photos.
l2c: Photograph only what it allows, or take no photo.
l3c: Point to one thing you did not photograph because of the rule or because a person did not agree.
safety: Taking a clear photo is a different skill.

name: Ask before you touch a display
description: Ask whether a display may be touched, and keep your hands off until the answer is yes.
l1c: Look for a touch or do-not-touch sign.
l2c: If there is no sign, ask a staff member.
l3c: Touch only after a yes, and describe what you were allowed to touch.
safety: Do not touch art, animals, or food samples unless you were told you may.

name: Record the name of a piece you liked
description: Write the name of a work you liked and one reason, so you can find it again.
l1c: Copy the title and the maker from the label.
l2c: Add one reason that points to something you saw or heard.
l3c: Later, use your note to find the work in a catalog or say the note was not enough and fix it.
safety: A review with evidence is a longer skill. Do not invent the title.

name: Hum a note and hold it
description: Choose a comfortable note, hum it, and stop when it wavers.
l1c: Hum a note that does not strain.
l2c: Hold it steadily for a short breath.
l3c: Stop when the note wavers or your throat tightens, and say which.
safety: Matching a pitch you heard is a different skill. Pain means stop.

name: Tap a rhythm and repeat it
description: Tap a short rhythm, then repeat it the same way.
l1c: Tap a short pattern and stop.
l1d: You can invent a short pattern.
l2c: Repeat the same pattern once.
l3c: Ask someone to tap it back, and say whether they matched it.
safety: Clapping a written rhythm is a different skill.

name: Fold a letter and put it in an envelope
description: Fold a letter so it fits an envelope and the greeting is what you see first when it opens.
l1c: Fold the letter so it fits the envelope without forcing.
l2c: Fold so the greeting is visible first when the reader opens it.
l3c: Seal a practice envelope or leave it unsealed for the post, and say which.
safety: Addressing for the post is a different skill.

name: Make a table of contents
description: Make a table of contents that matches the pages in a packet you assembled.
l1c: List the parts in the order they appear.
l2c: Add a page or a position for each part.
l3c: Open one part from the list and correct the list if it is wrong.
safety: Indexing a notebook is a different skill.

name: Color-code a shared calendar
description: Agree what calendar colors mean and use them on one week.
l1c: Agree what two colors mean with the other person.
l2c: Color one week using only those meanings.
l3c: If a color was used for two things, change one and tell the other person.
safety: Planning a week with buffers is a different skill. Do not rely on color alone.

name: Write an agenda item in one line
description: Write one agenda item so the group knows the outcome you want.
l1c: Write the topic in a few words.
l2c: Add the outcome, such as a decision, a list, or an update.
l2d: You can say what done is.
l3c: Add a time you will stop, and say what happens if you do not finish.
safety: Running the whole meeting is a different skill.

name: Collect questions before a talk
description: Collect questions before a talk so the speaker sees them in time.
l1c: Ask the group for questions before the talk starts.
l2c: Put two similar questions together and keep both names if they want.
l3c: Give the list to the speaker and say which question you did not understand well enough to group.
l3d: You can hand over an honest list.
safety: Do not drop a question because you dislike it.

name: Thank a host for a specific thing
description: Thank a host for something they actually did during the visit.
l1c: Name one thing the host did.
l2c: Say it to the host before you leave, or write it the same day.
l3c: Leave out a general compliment that could apply to any host.
safety: A written thank-you note is a close skill. This one is spoken or same-day and about the visit itself.

name: Offer water before a long task
description: Offer water before a long task and accept no.
l1c: Offer water and say where it is.
l2c: If they decline, do not insist.
l3c: If the task runs long, offer once more or point to the water, and stop there.
l3d: You can offer again without nagging.
safety: Do not give advice about health. Hosting a meal is a different skill.

name: Show where the toilets are
description: Tell or show a guest where the toilet is, including any step.
l1c: Check the way yourself before you send them.
l2c: Explain the turns, and mention a step if there is one.
l3c: Offer to walk with them, and stay if they say no.
l3d: You can let them go alone.
safety: Finding a step-free entrance is a different skill.

name: Agree who clears up
description: Agree who clears up after a shared task, before the task ends.
l1c: Ask who will clear up before everyone is tired.
l2c: Agree a split or one person, in a sentence.
l3c: Do the part you took, and say if you cannot.
safety: Loading a dishwasher is a different skill. Do not assume a guest will clean.

name: Tell a guest what they may use
description: Tell a guest what they may use in the kitchen or the room, and what to leave.
l1c: Name the things they may use.
l2c: Name one thing you would like left alone.
l3c: Point to one thing they should not switch on, such as a hob, if it matters, without a repair lesson.
safety: Do not teach them to repair appliances. Preparing a bed space is a different skill.

name: Measure a window for a covering
description: Measure a window's width and drop and write the numbers with the unit.
l1c: Measure the width at the place the covering would sit, and write the unit.
l2c: Measure the drop in the same unit.
l3n: Say what you did not decide
l3c: Say you have measurements, not a guarantee the covering will fit, until you check the product's own guide.
safety: Do not stand on an untested chair. Comparing products before buying is a different skill.

name: Read a detector card before you test it
description: Detector tests stay with the device card and with pack-09. No procedure is included. Kept for specialist review.
l1c: No procedure is included.
l1d: The idea stays for specialist review.
l2c: No performance criterion was written.
l2d: A specialist review can add a source later.
l3c: This record is not a pilot proposal.
l3d: It is not counted as a unique proposal.
safety: No procedure. Do not treat this record as instructions.
